answer.instructions: Which team should handle this customer support ticket?

criteria.account_access: Login problems, password resets, two-factor authentication, locked or suspended accounts, single sign-on issues
criteria.billing: Charges, invoices, refunds, payment methods, receipts, plan prices
criteria.bug_report: Something in the product is broken, throws errors, or behaves incorrectly
criteria.feature_request: Asks for new functionality or an improvement to how the product works
criteria.cancellation: Wants to cancel, close the account, stop auto-renewal, or leave the service

answer.instructions: Which emotion does the writer primarily express?

criteria.surprise: Astonishment or shock at something unexpected, without a dominant positive or negative feeling
criteria.disgust: Revulsion or strong distaste toward something gross or morally repugnant

answer.instructions: What is the main topic of this news article?

criteria.politics: Government, elections, legislation, diplomacy, political parties
criteria.science: Research discoveries, space, physics, biology, archaeology
criteria.health: Medicine, diseases, public health, hospitals, nutrition
criteria.technology: Gadgets, software, the internet, AI, cybersecurity, tech products
criteria.entertainment: Movies, music, TV, celebrities, games, books, arts
criteria.crime_justice: Crimes, police investigations, trials, court rulings
criteria.weather_environment: Weather events, natural disasters, climate, pollution, wildlife conservation

answer.instructions: Which cuisine does this recipe belong to?
Which scientific field does this paper primarily belong to?
What does the user want the assistant to do?

criteria.play_music: Start playing music, a song, artist or playlist
criteria.pause_music: Pause or stop music that is playing
criteria.set_alarm: Set a wake-up or clock alarm
criteria.weather_query: Ask about the weather or forecast
criteria.add_to_shopping_list: Add an item to the shopping list
criteria.check_camera: Show or check a security camera feed
criteria.read_calendar: Ask about scheduled events or appointments
criteria.other: Anything not covered by the options above

criteria.cardiology: Heart and blood vessels: chest pressure, palpitations, blood pressure
criteria.dermatology: Skin, hair and nails: rashes, moles, itching, acne
criteria.gastroenterology: Digestive system: stomach pain, reflux, bowel problems, liver
criteria.neurology: Brain and nerves: headaches, numbness, seizures, memory, dizziness
criteria.orthopedics: Bones, joints and muscles: fractures, sprains, back or knee pain
criteria.ophthalmology: Eyes and vision: blurred vision, eye pain, floaters, red eye

answer.instructions: Which language or technology is this question primarily about?
How should this forum comment be moderated?

criteria.acceptable: Normal on-topic contribution, including strong but civil disagreement
criteria.harassment: Insults, demeans or personally attacks another user
criteria.spam: Advertising, affiliate links, or unsolicited promotion
criteria.misinformation: States clearly false factual claims, e.g. health or science myths, as true
criteria.off_topic: Civil but unrelated to the thread's subject

answer.instructions: Which aspect of the hotel is this review mainly about?

criteria.staff_service: Reception, staff attitude, helpfulness, check-in experience
criteria.location: Neighborhood, distance to attractions, transport, surroundings
criteria.room_comfort: Bed, room size, furniture, temperature, view
criteria.other: Anything else (e.g. pool, parking, wifi, gym)

answer.instructions: How severe is the reported bug?
criteria: Cosmetic: a visual or wording problem; functionality is unaffected
Minor: a feature misbehaves in an edge case or is inconvenient, and an easy workaround exists
Major: a core feature is broken or gives wrong results for many users; workarounds are painful or partial
Critical: crash, data loss, security hole, or the whole product is unusable, with no workaround

answer.instructions: How frustrated is the customer?
criteria: Calm and neutral: no sign of annoyance
Mildly inconvenienced: slight annoyance but patient and friendly
Clearly frustrated: complains about the problem and expresses dissatisfaction
Very frustrated: mentions repeated failures, strong complaints, patience running out
Furious: hostile, threatens to leave or escalate, may use all caps or insults

answer.instructions: How formal is the language of this text?
criteria: Very informal: slang, abbreviations, emojis, no capitalization, chat-style
Casual: relaxed everyday language with contractions and a friendly tone
Neutral: standard, clear language suitable for most contexts
Formal: professional register, complete sentences, polite conventions, few contractions
Very formal: ceremonial or legalistic language, elaborate courtesy, rigid structure

answer.instructions: What audience is this explanation written for, based on its technical complexity?
criteria: For a young child: everyday words and analogies, no technical terms
For a general adult audience: a few technical terms, each explained
For a knowledgeable hobbyist or student: uses field terminology without explaining the basics
For experts: dense jargon, formulas or specialized notation, assumes deep background

answer.instructions: How polite is this email request?
criteria: Rude: demanding, insulting, or dismissive
Curt: blunt demand with no greeting or thanks
Neutral: plain request with basic courtesy
Polite: greeting, please/thank you, considerate tone
Very polite: highly deferential, apologizes for imposing, elaborate gratitude

answer.instructions: How urgent is this helpdesk request?
criteria: Can wait: a question or minor request with no deadline and little impact
Soon: affects someone's work or has a deadline within days
Immediate: work is stopped for many people, a security incident, or a deadline within hours

answer.instructions: How well does the answer address the question that was asked? (Judge relevance and completeness, not factual accuracy.)
criteria: Does not address the question at all: off-topic or a refusal
Touches the topic but does not answer what was asked
Partially answers: addresses the question but misses an important part
Fully answers the question directly and completely

answer.instructions: What star rating does this review most likely correspond to?
criteria: 1 star: very negative; the product failed or is terrible; would not recommend
2 stars: mostly negative with a minor positive
3 stars: mixed or mediocre; pros and cons balance out
4 stars: mostly positive with minor complaints
5 stars: enthusiastic, no real complaints

answer.instructions: How risky is the described outdoor activity for the people involved?
criteria: Negligible risk: routine activity in safe conditions
Low risk: minor hazards that are well managed
Elevated risk: notable hazards or missing precautions that could cause injury
Severe risk: conditions or behavior likely to cause serious injury or death

answer.instructions: How experienced in the hobby is the person who wrote this post?
criteria: Complete beginner: brand new, does not know basic terminology
Novice: knows a few basic terms but struggles with fundamentals
Advanced beginner: understands the basics and is learning to apply them
Intermediate: comfortable with core techniques, working on refinement
Advanced amateur: deep technical knowledge, specialized equipment, consistent results
Semi-professional: occasionally paid for the work, discusses workflow and clients
Seasoned expert: many years of experience, teaches others, industry-level nuance

answer.instructions: Is the customer asking for a refund (their money back)?

criteria.true: Explicitly or implicitly asks to get their money returned
criteria.false: Asks for something else (replacement, repair, exchange, store credit, information), or mentions refunds without requesting one

answer.instructions: Does the text contain personal data that identifies or contacts a specific private individual?

criteria.true: Contains at least one of: a personal phone number, personal email address, home street address, government ID number, bank or card number, or a full name together with a date of birth
criteria.false: No such data; first names alone, public figures, company phone numbers, or generic addresses like support@company.com do not count

answer.instructions: Does the passage contain the information needed to answer the question?

criteria.true: The answer can be found in or directly inferred from the passage
criteria.false: The passage does not provide the answer, even if it is on a related topic

answer.instructions: Is the claim fully supported by the source?

criteria.true: Everything in the claim is stated in or directly entailed by the source
criteria.false: The claim contradicts the source, adds details not in it, or overgeneralizes

answer.instructions: Do the two records describe the same product (same model and same variant)?

criteria.true: Same product, model and variant, even if written differently
criteria.false: Different product, model, size, capacity, color or version

answer.instructions: Is this email a phishing attempt?

criteria.true: Tries to trick the recipient into revealing credentials, paying, opening a malicious link/attachment, or impersonates someone
criteria.false: Legitimate email, even if urgent or promotional

answer.instructions: Does the review mention a problem with shipping or delivery?

criteria.true: Late, lost, damaged in transit, delivered to the wrong place, or other delivery issues
criteria.false: No delivery problem (product defects, quality or fit issues do not count)

answer.instructions: Is the user asking to talk to a human agent?

criteria.true: Requests a person, live agent, representative or phone call with staff
criteria.false: Anything else, including complaints about the bot without asking for a person

answer.instructions: Do these meeting notes assign a specific task to a specific person?

criteria.true: A named person (or clearly identified individual) is responsible for a concrete action
criteria.false: No owner for any action (only discussion, decisions, or 'someone should...')

answer.instructions: Has the main event described in the text already taken place?

criteria.true: The event actually happened in the past
criteria.false: The event is planned, expected, hypothetical, cancelled, postponed, or did not happen

sentiment.instructions: How bullish or bearish is this tweet about the stock mentioned, considering both the author's view and the news it reports?
criteria: Strongly bearish: the author's view or the reported news points clearly to a large fall (selling, shorting, severe bad news)
Mildly bearish: leans negative; suggests some decline or underperformance
Neutral: no directional implication (routine or in-line news, balanced views, or undecided)
Mildly bullish: leans positive; suggests some gains
Strongly bullish: the author's view or the reported news points clearly to a large rise (buying heavily, hype, major good news)

direction.instructions: Which direction does this tweet suggest for the stock price?

criteria.bearish: Suggests the price will go down
criteria.bullish: Suggests the price will go up

expects_rise.instructions: Does this tweet suggest the stock price will rise?

criteria.true: The author's view or the reported news points to a price increase
criteria.false: It points to a decline, or has no clear direction
